text.headline: Timeline of Brazil
text.text: Major events in the history of Brazil.

events.headline: Arrival of the Portuguese
events.text: The Portuguese arrived in Brazil in 1500, led by Pedro Álvares Cabral. This marked the beginning of European colonization in the region.

events.headline: Establishment of Sugar Plantations
events.text: The establishment of sugar plantations in Brazil began in the 1530s, leading to the importation of African slaves. This became a cornerstone of the Brazilian economy.

events.headline: Foundation of Salvador
events.text: Salvador was founded as the first capital of Brazil in 1549. It became a major center for the Portuguese colonial administration.

events.headline: Independence from Portugal
events.text: Brazil declared independence from Portugal on September 7, 1822, led by Dom Pedro I. This event marked the end of colonial rule in Brazil.

events.headline: Abolition of Slavery
events.text: Brazil became the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery on May 13, 1888, with the signing of the Lei Áurea. This was a significant step towards social reform.

events.headline: Proclamation of the Republic
events.text: On November 15, 1889, Brazil was declared a republic, ending the monarchy of Dom Pedro II. This marked the beginning of a new political era.

events.headline: Getúlio Vargas Comes to Power
events.text: Getúlio Vargas seized power in a coup in 1930, initiating a period of authoritarian rule known as the Vargas Era. His policies transformed Brazil's economy and society.

events.headline: End of Vargas Era
events.text: The Vargas Era ended in 1945 when Vargas was ousted from power. This led to a return to democracy and the establishment of a new constitution.

events.headline: Military Coup
events.text: On April 1, 1964, a military coup d'état overthrew the democratically elected government of João Goulart. This initiated a period of military dictatorship that lasted until 1985.

events.headline: Return to Democracy
events.text: In 1985, Brazil transitioned back to democracy after 21 years of military rule. This was marked by the election of Tancredo Neves as president.

events.headline: Introduction of the Real Plan
events.text: The Real Plan was introduced in 1994 to stabilize the Brazilian economy and curb hyperinflation. It successfully established the Brazilian real as the national currency.

events.headline: Election of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
events.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was elected president in 2002, marking a significant shift in Brazilian politics. His administration focused on social programs and poverty reduction.

events.headline: Election of Dilma Rousseff
events.text: Dilma Rousseff was elected as Brazil's first female president in 2010. Her presidency focused on social policies and economic growth.

events.headline: Impeachment of Dilma Rousseff
events.text: In 2016, Dilma Rousseff was impeached and removed from office on charges of fiscal mismanagement. This event sparked widespread protests and political turmoil.

events.headline: Election of Jair Bolsonaro
events.text: Jair Bolsonaro was elected president in 2018, representing a shift towards right-wing politics in Brazil. His administration faced criticism for its handling of environmental and social issues.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted Brazil in 2020, leading to a public health crisis and economic challenges. The government faced criticism for its response to the pandemic.

events.headline: Election of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (again)
events.text: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was elected president again in 2022, defeating incumbent Jair Bolsonaro. His return to power marked a significant political shift in Brazil.
